text:
maria: Quick heads-up, running terraform plan for payments microservice and KMS grants show the aws_kms_grant being replaced. IRSA role resource unchanged.
jonathan: can you paste the plan diff? :eyes:
maria: Sure, snippet:
```
~ aws_kms_grant.payments_encrypt
    grantee_principal: "arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/payments-irsa" => "arn:aws:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/payments-irsa/web-prod-abc"
```
li: ah yea that's the classic principal canonicalization flip — something in how the role ARN is being referenced (maybe we switched to data.aws_caller_identity or used an assumed-role output). TF sees the assumed-role ARN and wants to replace the grant.
sam: we've hit this before when the deploy tool started passing the assumed principal instead of the role arn (helm values or k8s annotations accidentally included session name).
jonathan: options: 1) reference the role ARN directly (aws_iam_role.payments.arn) for grantee_principal 2) move permission into the kms key policy instead of using an aws_kms_grant 3) add lifecycle { ignore_changes = ["grantee_principal"] } on the grant to avoid churn.
li: i prefer 1 + a short code comment. key policy changes are noisy and ignore_changes just hides drift.
maria: i'll switch module input to use aws_iam_role.payments.arn (instead of whatever the CI script was passing) and re-run plan.
tf-bot: terraform plan finished with 13 changes (2 to add, 11 to change). :white_check_mark:
maria: pushed change and re-ran plan, looks clean now — no replace for kms grant. thanks all! :shipit:
jonathan: nice. can you open a tiny PR to document why we reference role.arn (so future devs don't reintroduce this)?
maria: yep will do, linking in #pr-reviews when ready.
